principle_text: When the seller emphasizes the item's condition without addressing pricing, avoid engaging in non-essential discussions and steer the conversation back to negotiating a lower price.
When the buyer expresses affordability concerns without specifying a counteroffer, avoid engaging in open-ended questions about their budget to prevent potential anchoring at a higher price.
When the buyer references competitive pricing and anchors their offer at a low price, you should consider adjusting your price slightly lower to show flexibility and willingness to negotiate.

When the seller emphasizes product features without addressing pricing, avoid showing minimal interest or confirmation responses to prevent reinforcing the initial asking price without progressing in negotiation.
When the seller emphasizes the offer's strengths without addressing pricing terms, avoid reiterating interest without introducing new leverage or price discussion.

When the seller confirms the product includes only the frame, you should leverage this information to negotiate a lower price or request additional value like the included mattresses for the same price.
When the buyer asks about an item already specified in the description, avoid reiterating the same information to maintain negotiation focus on price-related details.
When the seller maintains the initial price without offering concessions, avoid making vague negotiation requests without specifying terms or a counteroffer.
When the seller acknowledges heavy use of the item and its high initial cost, you should continue to highlight any flaws or issues to negotiate a lower price effectively.
When the seller emphasizes the value and uniqueness of the item, avoid making a direct inquiry about the price without introducing negotiation tactics or concessions.
When the seller shows disinterest or prematurely closes the conversation, avoid re-engaging without presenting specific offers or negotiating points to prevent unproductive exchanges.
When the seller emphasizes the features of the home instead of addressing buyer inquiries, avoid deflecting questions about nearby amenities or other non-price related aspects.

When the seller highlights positive features of the property without indicating willingness to adjust the price, avoid making inquiries solely about the condition of the house as it may not lead to immediate progress in negotiating a lower price.
When the seller offers a lower counteroffer in response to the buyer's firm initial price, you should maintain your anchor and negotiate further to secure a better deal.
When the seller states the initial price, avoid immediately accepting it without attempting to negotiate or make a counteroffer.
When the buyer requests time to review the product without making an offer or asking for a discount, avoid restating the initial price without any further negotiation or concession.
When the seller emphasizes the positive attributes of the room without addressing price negotiation, avoid discussing only the features and location to prevent leaving the buyer's leverage unchanged.

When the seller states the price without acknowledging or reacting to the buyer's positive feedback on the property, avoid missing the opportunity to engage in price negotiation based on the buyer's interest and needs.
When the seller asks about questions or concerns, avoid failing to introduce price negotiation or leverage to make progress towards a lower price.
When the seller sets a high starting price without any concession or counteroffer, avoid making generic statements like 'Yes I am' that do not directly address price negotiation.
When the seller is not interested in trades, you should acknowledge the buyer's cash offer and negotiate based on the proposed price to move the discussion forward effectively.
When the seller states the initial price without concession, avoid making vague statements about budget constraints without following up with a specific counteroffer or negotiation proposal.
When the seller hints at the possibility of a better deal for multiple units, you should explore negotiating for a bulk discount to leverage quantity for a lower price.
When the seller offers an amazing deal without specifying details, avoid failing to introduce negotiation terms or leverage to improve your position.
When discussing delivery options, avoid confirming additional fees without linking them to potential price adjustments, as it may limit your ability to negotiate a lower price.
When the seller shows willingness to come down in price, you should continue negotiating and pushing for further concessions to achieve a better deal.

When the seller maintains the initial price but offers non-price concessions like delivery and warranty, avoid asking for the best price without introducing new negotiation leverage to prompt a price reduction.
When the buyer challenges the price by stating it's too high, the seller should directly ask for the buyer's counteroffer to prompt negotiation and create leverage for proposing a lower amount.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition, avoid making no further progress in negotiation and not leveraging this information to potentially lower the price.
When the seller emphasizes the beauty of the area, avoid asking questions that do not directly address price negotiation to maintain focus on securing a lower price.
When the seller agrees that a price is fair, you should continue negotiating to secure a more favorable deal rather than settling too quickly.
When the buyer offers to handle transportation and reduces the price, you should consider accepting the lower offer to improve the buyer's terms and potentially secure a better deal.

When the seller indicates openness to negotiate by expressing willingness to work with a slightly lower offer, you should propose a reasonable price close to your budget to advance the negotiation effectively.

When the seller shows willingness to accept a lower price contingent on logistical convenience, you should offer to reduce their effort by handling pickup or meeting arrangements to strengthen your negotiation position.
When the seller clearly states a firm minimum price close to their initial asking price, avoid making offers significantly below your own initial price as it weakens your negotiating leverage.

When the seller responds with a tentative willingness to lower the price, you should clearly express your concern about the high price and directly ask for a specific reduction to encourage further concessions.
When the seller confirms logistical details without addressing price, avoid making concessions that do not advance price negotiations or leverage.
When the seller responds positively to compliments without discussing price, avoid repeating compliments without introducing negotiation or price inquiries.
When the seller provides detailed product information without mentioning price flexibility, avoid making demands or aggressive price concessions prematurely.
When the seller has set a firm initial price, avoid praising it as generous or implying disbelief, as this can weaken your negotiating leverage and confuse your intent to negotiate a lower price.
When the seller asks for your price range and emphasizes the property's value, avoid making vague statements without a specific counteroffer or clear price proposal.
When the seller responds to a low price offer by shifting focus to logistical conditions, you should use this as leverage to negotiate additional concessions or confirm buyer commitment.
When the seller has firmly stated the price and emphasized the item's good condition, avoid asking questions that only confirm quality without addressing price or terms.
When the seller has stated the item condition and firm price, avoid responding with minimal affirmations that do not engage or advance the negotiation.
When the seller emphasizes the item's excellent condition without addressing the buyer's stated budget, avoid ignoring the buyer's price anchor to prevent losing negotiation leverage.
When the seller confirms the item is in very good condition with only normal wear, avoid focusing solely on condition inquiries that do not create leverage for price negotiation.
When the seller provides detailed product features without mentioning price, avoid asking questions that focus solely on functionality instead of steering the conversation toward price negotiation.
When the seller confirms product features that reinforce its value, avoid asking questions unrelated to price negotiation as they do not help in securing a better price.

When the seller firmly justifies a high asking price by highlighting recent upgrades and neighborhood value, avoid making an aggressive lowball offer that undermines your credibility and stalls negotiation.
When the seller indicates the item is recently acquired and affirms its quality without mentioning price, avoid asking questions that do not directly create leverage for a price concession.
When the seller immediately accepts an offer close to their initial price, avoid making concessions that reduce your negotiating leverage and increase the final price.
When the seller confirms a product limitation that reduces its value, you should ask clarifying questions to gather information that supports negotiating a lower price.
When the seller has only expressed enthusiasm without discussing price or concessions, avoid focusing solely on product features without linking them to price negotiation.
When the seller reaffirms the item's excellent condition and counters with a higher price, you should avoid expressing uncertainty about the item's quality to maintain leverage in price negotiation.
When the seller defers detailed information to a third party but permits property viewing, avoid pressing prematurely for price concessions before assessing the property’s condition and value.
When the seller invites you to propose a price after you offer logistical help, avoid delaying your price offer and instead present a clear price expectation to advance the negotiation.
When the seller responds with a counteroffer significantly above your initial target price, avoid making an opening offer below your own initial price as it weakens your negotiation leverage.
When the seller clearly states the item for sale, avoid introducing unrelated items that confuse the negotiation and hinder progress toward price agreement.

When the seller states their lowest acceptable price and mentions additional costs they bear, you should politely acknowledge the fairness and then request a slight price reduction to encourage a better offer.
When the seller provides factual information about the item's usage history without adjusting price, avoid making inquiries that do not directly advance price negotiation or leverage.
When the seller acknowledges your willingness to accommodate logistical details without adjusting the price, avoid assuming this immediately improves your bargaining position.

When the seller responds to a buyer's initial price offer by proposing a compromise price between the buyer's offer and their own, you should make an aggressive counteroffer below your initial target price to create downward pressure.
When the seller responds to a low buyer offer by raising the price and adding extras, avoid making offers below your stated initial price as it weakens your negotiation position.

When the seller emphasizes the property's luxury features and maintains a firm price despite your budget constraints, avoid shifting focus to unrelated concessions that do not directly pressure the price downward.
When the seller emphasizes the item's excellent condition and low mileage, avoid focusing solely on general interest without addressing price or value to advance the negotiation.
When the seller provides neutral factual information without discussing price, avoid focusing solely on non-price details that do not advance the negotiation leverage.
When the seller states a firm, non-negotiable policy that conflicts with the buyer's disclosed needs, avoid introducing deal-breaking information early that limits negotiation possibilities.
When the seller confirms the item is in good condition and mentions logistical constraints without adjusting price, avoid focusing solely on condition inquiries without addressing price or terms.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition and shares a personal reason for selling, avoid asking only about item issues without leveraging that information for price negotiation.
When the seller denies defects and shifts the conversation to your budget, avoid asking questions that do not directly create leverage for lowering the price.
When the seller states a high initial price but shows willingness to negotiate, you should clearly anchor with a lower target price to prompt a seller concession.
When the seller confirms the item is in good condition without indicating flexibility, avoid relying solely on condition inquiries to lower the price early in the negotiation.
When the seller clearly states their initial asking price without signaling flexibility, avoid merely confirming the price without introducing negotiation tactics or offers to influence the price.
When the seller responds with a conditional price reduction tied to lease terms, avoid opening negotiations without presenting a clear counteroffer or position to strengthen your bargaining leverage.
When the seller indicates the price is firm and expects reasonable offers, avoid making vague or unspecific requests for a lower price without proposing concrete terms or concessions.
When the seller provides factual information unrelated to price or concessions, avoid focusing solely on non-price details that do not advance the negotiation leverage or pricing discussion.
When the seller clarifies a discrepancy in the item description without adjusting the price, avoid ignoring the opportunity to leverage this inconsistency to negotiate a better deal.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition with no significant issues, avoid asking questions that do not directly contribute to negotiating a better price.
When the seller emphasizes the item's good condition and reason for selling without mentioning price, avoid making inquiries that do not create leverage or prompt price concessions.
When the seller's last response indicates confusion or a misunderstanding about the buyer's intent, avoid making off-topic or unrelated statements that do not advance the price negotiation.
When the seller expresses interest but maintains a high initial price, you should acknowledge interest while signaling price constraints to prompt the seller to ask for your specific price range.
When the seller provides detailed product features without indicating price flexibility, avoid making purely informational requests that do not advance price negotiation.
When the seller confirms minimal use and no issues with the product, avoid asking questions that allow the seller to reinforce the item's value without creating leverage for a price reduction.
When the seller discloses minor flaws transparently and downplays their impact, you should ask for specific details to gather leverage for negotiating a lower price.

When the seller provides detailed information about the item's condition and personal context without addressing price, avoid making vague or non-committal statements that do not advance the negotiation.
When the seller acknowledges the product's quality but hints at some price flexibility, you should express price concerns to encourage the seller to consider lowering their price.
When the seller has made a reasonable initial price offer, avoid making counteroffers that are significantly higher and inconsistent with the negotiation context, as this weakens your position.

When the seller acknowledges the item's used condition but emphasizes good quality and offers a bargain price, you should ask questions that highlight usage duration to encourage early price concessions.
When the seller confirms they offer the service you need without discussing price, avoid making statements that do not introduce negotiation or price-related information.
When the seller confirms the item is in great condition with only normal wear, avoid accepting this information without probing for any possible flaws or negotiating price based solely on condition.
When the seller confirms the item is brand new and in perfect condition, avoid focusing solely on product condition questions that do not advance price negotiation or create leverage.
When the seller asks about your budget after a vague response, avoid giving non-committal answers that fail to establish clear leverage or guide the negotiation toward a better price.
When the seller confirms the item is brand new and in excellent condition, avoid asking only about condition without linking it to price negotiation or leverage.
When the seller responds by emphasizing the property's positive features without addressing price, avoid merely expressing generic interest without introducing price or negotiation terms.
When the seller emphasizes the high quality of the item without addressing concerns, avoid introducing personal setbacks that do not directly influence price negotiation.
When the seller reiterates their initial price without concession, avoid merely confirming interest without making a counteroffer or applying negotiation pressure.
